reconcile.connective: Defenders limit the Deuteronomic prohibition — it guarded the fruit-trees of Canaan, the land Israel would settle, and did not bind the punitive devastation of Moab.

discrepancy.connective: Steve Wells (Skeptic's Annotated Bible) presses the tension at face value, simply juxtaposing the Deuteronomic 'thou shalt not destroy the trees' with Elisha's command through Yahweh's prophet to 'fell every good tree' against Moab.

skeptic.name: Steve Wells
skeptic.work: Skeptic's Annotated Bible, "Were the Israelites to spare the trees in the countries they invaded?" (save_trees.html)

excerpts.excerpt_text: In the announcement of the devastation of the land there is an allusion to Deu 20:19-20, according to which the Israelites were ordered to spare the fruit-trees when Canaan was taken. These instructions were not to apply to Moab, because the Moabites themselves as the arch-foes of Israel would not act in any other way with the land of Israel if they should gain the victory.
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Directly names BOTH passages and states the harmonization: the Deut 20:19-20 fruit-tree law was specific to the taking of Canaan and did not bind the punitive war on Moab. The single strongest, most explicit reconcile on the row; the on-tension sentence sits in the Kg2 3:18-19 sub-block of this anchor note.

pd_work.resource: Keil & Delitzsch, Biblical Commentary on the Old Testament (1861-75), on 2 Kings 3:18-19
pd_work.author: Keil & Delitzsch
pd_work.note: Treats this exact pair, reading 2 Kings 3:19 as an allusion to Deut 20:19-20 whose fruit-tree protection was specific to the taking of Canaan and not binding on the punitive war against Moab. Row-surfaced harmonizing commentator keyed to the passage; Haley's specific coverage of this pair unconfirmed.

link.title: Defending Inerrancy: 2 Kings 3:18-19 — Didn't Israel violate the law of warfare by destroying fruit trees?
link.note: Live apologetic page citing both Deut 20:19 and 2 Kings 3:18-19; harmonizes via scope-of-the-law and the Canaan-vs-Moab territorial distinction.
